Diagnosis.Cancer Type: adenocarcinoma of the tail of the pancreas

Surgery Information.Surgery Findings: moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with negative margins and 2 of 29 lymph nodes were positive

Symptoms or Side Effects.Side Effect: severe adverse events including metabolic abnormalities with hypercalcemia and hyponatremia as well as total body aches
severe hand-foot syndrome with cracking and blistering
falls associated with loss of balance

Additional Comments: The patient is a 65-year-old woman with a history of adenocarcinoma of the tail of the pancreas, status post distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy with positive lymph nodes. She has experienced severe adverse effects from chemotherapy, including hand-foot syndrome and mucositis, leading to the temporary cessation of treatment. She has also been dealing with frequent falls and balance issues, for which a CT of the head was unremarkable. She is currently using a walker to aid with mobility. Additionally, she has been started on Lovenox for an incidental pulmonary embolism and will undergo Doppler studies to check for deep vein thrombosis. She has a history of psoriatic arthritis, chronic asthma, hypertension, and previous MRSA infections. Her current medications for supportive care include Tylenol, Flexeril, and gabapentin for musculoskeletal pain.
